repo_notes.content: Rigor is a type-aware static bug finder for Ruby that requires zero annotations and imposes zero runtime dependencies. It parses code using Prism and infers types directly from the values produced by expressions. Key architectural commitments: (1) Types are facts, not wishes: types are derived from actual execution semantics rather than aspirational comments; (2) False positives outrank worst-case static reading: findings fire only when the receiver type is conclusively known and evidence is sound (tested against corpora like Mastodon, Redmine, GitLab FOSS); (3) Programmable inference beyond unions: tracks literal values, integer ranges, refinements (e.g., non-empty-string), tuple and hash shapes, and effect labels.
repo_notes.author: Rigor Maintainers

repo_notes.content: Domain glossary and terminology traps (defined in CONTEXT.md): (1) 'interface' ALWAYS means structural typing (like Go interfaces or Python Protocols; satisfied by methods, no 'implements' clause); never Java/PHP nominal interfaces. (2) 'protocol' is strictly reserved for ADR-28 path-scoped behavioral method contracts in plugin manifests. (3) 'scope' is overloaded: Rigor::Scope is the immutable inference state; 'analysis scope' is the set of files analyzed in a run; 'publish set' is the LSP notification target. (4) 'Dynamic[T]' is gradual typing ('statically unknown, believed within envelope T') and carries a dynamic origin explaining why it is dynamic (ADR-75, ADR-82). (5) 'erasure' is the conservative mapping of rich internal carriers back to standard RBS.
repo_notes.author: Rigor Maintainers

repo_notes.content: Repository layout and documentation authority: (1) Normative specifications: docs/type-specification/ (type system) and docs/internal-spec/ (inference engine contracts) are binding. (2) Architecture Decision Records: docs/adr/ explains the rationale behind architectural decisions; docs/adr/README.md is the complete index. (3) Core implementation lives in lib/rigor/ (engine, CLI, language server, MCP server, cache, effects). (4) Production framework plugins live in plugins/ (Rails, ActiveRecord, RSpec, Sorbet bridge, Sidekiq, Devise, dry-rb, and more; plugins/README.md is the inventory); examples/ holds plugin-contract walkthroughs, not production support. (5) User-facing agent skills that Rigor ships to adopting projects live in skills/ (e.g. rigor-next-steps, rigor-ask, rigor-project-init; skills/README.md is the inventory); .claude/skills/ holds contributor-only workflows for this repository and is not part of the product. Upstream submodules in references/ are read-only upstream material.
repo_notes.author: Rigor Maintainers

repo_notes.content: Keep this wiki pointing at indexes rather than restating them: do not enumerate ADR numbers, class names, file paths below a namespace, or counts of plugins/rules/skills. Read the current set from docs/adr/README.md (ADRs and their status), docs/agents/code-map.md (what each lib/rigor/ namespace owns), plugins/README.md, skills/README.md, and docs/manual/README.md. docs/notes/ and docs/design/ are non-normative, time-stamped notes; a note under a '> **Historical**' banner is spent and superseded, so do not present it as current behaviour.
repo_notes.author: Rigor Maintainers

pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: What Rigor is, its design boundaries (inference-first, no inline annotations, zero runtime dependency, false positives weighed above worst-case reading), and how the major subsystems below relate.

page_notes.content: Start from README.md, AGENTS.md, CONTEXT.md and docs/adr/0-concept.md. Rigor is a static bug finder, not a type-system compiler or runtime checker.

pages.title: Using Rigor
pages.purpose: Installation, configuration (.rigor.yml / .rigor.dist.yml), the CLI commands, diagnostics, baselines, CI, editor (LSP) and agent (MCP, bundled skills) integrations, as a user adopting Rigor sees them.

page_notes.content: Follow docs/manual/README.md (chapter index) and docs/install.md; the configuration schema is schemas/rigor-config.schema.json. Rigor runs as a global tool on its own Ruby while analysing code for any Ruby version.

pages.title: Type System
pages.purpose: Rigor's type model: an RBS superset with value-precise carriers, certainty, refinements, RBS consumption and erasure, and the RBS::Extended annotation surface.

page_notes.content: The binding source is docs/type-specification/README.md; rationale is in ADR-1 and ADR-3 and the ADRs docs/adr/README.md lists. docs/types.md is the informational summary. Code locations: docs/agents/code-map.md.

pages.title: Inference Engine
pages.purpose: The flow-sensitive inference pipeline: walking Prism ASTs, threading the immutable Scope through statements, narrowing, and the tiered method dispatcher that resolves return types.

page_notes.content: The binding contract is docs/internal-spec/README.md (start with inference-engine.md); ADR-4 explains the design. Dispatch tier order is normative. Use docs/agents/code-map.md for which file owns each part.

pages.title: Analysis, Diagnostics and Reports
pages.purpose: How a check run is orchestrated (discovery, parsing, rule application, suppression, severity profiles, parallel workers, incremental runs) and the other analysis reports: baseline and triage, type-protection coverage, effect labels, and unused-code reachability.

page_notes.content: Diagnostic policy is docs/type-specification/diagnostic-policy.md; user-facing behaviour is in the docs/manual/ chapters. Find the owning namespace in docs/agents/code-map.md and the governing ADRs in docs/adr/README.md.

pages.title: Plugins
pages.purpose: The plugin extension API and the production plugins that teach Rigor about frameworks and metaprogramming (Rails, testing, ecosystem gems, Sorbet bridge) without changing analysed code.

page_notes.content: The contract is ADR-2 and docs/manual/07-plugins.md; plugins/README.md is the authoritative inventory (do not state a count) and examples/README.md lists the contract walkthroughs.

pages.title: Environment and Caching
pages.purpose: Rigor::Environment as the facade over loaded RBS, class registry and project signatures, and the persistent disk cache with its invalidation rules.

page_notes.content: The cache contract is docs/internal-spec/cache.md; the user view is docs/manual/12-caching.md. Code locations: docs/agents/code-map.md.

pages.title: Contributing
pages.purpose: Development setup through the Nix Flake, the targeted local validation and the CI gate, and the branch, pull-request and release flow.

page_notes.content: AGENTS.md is the contract: every command through 'nix develop --command <cmd>', 'make verify-quick' / 'make verify-changed' locally, never the full suite (CI runs it). The flow is in CONTRIBUTING.md and docs/agents/contribution-flow.md.
